t: You're looking at the memorial to W. H. Hudson, a sculpture by Jacob Epstein, with Eric Gill also credited as a maker. Hudson was an Anglo-Argentine author and naturalist, born on the Argentine pampas, where he roamed freely as a boy and watched birds. Two Patagonian species carry his name. His most popular book, Green Mansions, from 1904, is a romance set in the Venezuelan forest. Epstein was born in the United States, moved to Europe in 1902, and became a British subject in 1910.
